A stub returning a scored document row with score between 0.16 and 0.5 would pin it.

justifications.durability: the guard is shown to fire rather than merely green: the base arm fails the two new tests against the literal-threshold source, and restoring the runner literal 0.5 makes test_pending_ingest_uses_content_cutoff fail (negative-control.log). The runner test asserts the query binds $min_score equal to the shared constant, which pins the binding rather than a value, so a future re-literalisation is caught. Deduction: the second literal comparison the worker also fixed — the document pending count at parallel.py:1106 — has no direct test, so reverting only that line to 0.5 would not be caught (recorded as a follow-on).
justifications.evidence: the reviewed run carries a reproducing baseline (baseline-threshold.log: 2 failed, 1 warning, EXIT=1 at base f186f51a) whose two failures are exactly the two named displays reading the literals, a head gate (gate-committed.log: 51 passed, EXIT=0 at head fa5123a2), and a mutation control (negative-control.log: 1 failed, 1 passed, EXIT=1 restoring literal 0.5 in the runner query). I opened all three logs and independently re-ran the scoped gate at head in the reviewed worktree (reviewer-head.log: 51 passed, EXIT=0), so the head arm reproduces. Deduction: the label half of the negative control rests on the baseline arm rather than a fresh mutation, and the reviewed run's own control mutated only the runner query.
justifications.fit: the commit subject 'fix(wiki): align progress thresholds with content ingest gate' uses conventional form and carries a body stating what changed and why; the added symbols (test_pending_ingest_uses_content_cutoff, test_document_label_uses_content_cutoff) name the mechanism; the new test filename describes what it tests. No plan, sprint, ticket or phase identifier appears in the diff, message, docstrings or comments, and the commit carries no attribution trailer.
justifications.goal_fidelity: §18 asks that the wiki runner's pending-ingest status in imas_codex/discovery/wiki/parallel.py and the document skipped label in imas_codex/discovery/wiki/progress.py stop comparing against the retired 0.5 language-model threshold and read CONTENT_INGEST_THRESHOLD instead, with a test that fails if either compares against a literal. The committed query at parallel.py:1028 now binds `wp.score_composite >= $min_score` with min_score=CONTENT_INGEST_THRESHOLD (parallel.py:1031), the same function's document pending count compares r["score"] >= CONTENT_INGEST_THRESHOLD (parallel.py:1106), and the label at progress.py:743 tests document.score_composite < CONTENT_INGEST_THRESHOLD. The constant resolves to 0.16 at graph_ops.py:29, the value §5 moved ingest to. Both done-when clauses hold.
justifications.reuse: the change routes both displays through the existing single source of truth CONTENT_INGEST_THRESHOLD already imported by parallel.py:31 and defined at graph_ops.py:29, rather than introducing a second constant or a local threshold. The new tests import the same constant, so the test and the code under test cannot drift apart.
justifications.scope_discipline: git show --stat fa5123a2 lists exactly imas_codex/discovery/wiki/parallel.py, imas_codex/discovery/wiki/progress.py and tests/wiki/test_wiki_threshold_displays.py — the three paths the manifest declares in changed_paths and orientation_write_paths. No CLI default, facility-independent of the runner, was touched, matching the plan's note that the CLI defaults are a separate node's scope. The worktree is clean at the reviewed head.
